title: NASA's Crew-13 aims for fastest U.S. trip to the space station
summary:
NASA planned to send four people to the International Space Station, and the trip could set a record. The mission is called Crew-13. A SpaceX Dragon spacecraft was scheduled to lift off at 11:10 a.m. EDT on Thursday, Oct. 1, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

Docking with the station was targeted for about 7 p.m. The trip from launch to docking was planned to take 7 hours and 50 minutes. If it happened as scheduled, it would be the fastest trip to the space station by a U.S. spacecraft in the station's history.

Four crew members were to fly on Dragon. They are NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov. A cosmonaut is a space traveler from Russia. They will spend an extended period aboard the station doing science and other mission activities.

NASA planned to show the launch and arrival live on several platforms. After arriving, the new crew will do a brief handover with members of NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 mission. A handover is when one crew passes along information to the next. Crew-12 is expected to begin its trip back to Earth no earlier than Monday, Oct. 5. All times were Eastern and could change based on real-time operations.
why_it_matters: Trips to the space station carry astronauts and science work to a laboratory in orbit. A faster trip would show how spaceflight planning is improving.
